newsitem.title: CHINA: Poor debut leads Shenzhen B index on dive at noon.
newsitem.headline: Poor debut leads Shenzhen B index on dive at noon.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares lost heavily on Tuesday morning led by an unusually weak debut by Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, analysts said.
The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index plunged 6.43 points or 5.04 percent to 121.26 on turnover of HK$74.1 million.
The domestic currency A share index fell 13.58 points or 3.59 percent to 364.77 points compounding the battering confidence had already taken from recent plunges, brokers said.
Turnover in the A share market was 2.3 billion yuan.
Bengang ended the morning at HK$1.96, down 17.65 percent from the offer price of HK$2.38 and becoming the first new share this year to suffer on the first trading day.
"This is sending very bad signals to the market," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Market confidence was hit after Hong Kong's transition to Beijing rule on July 1 failed to lift markets as expected, analysts said.
Shenzhen's A and B shares have been hit by a long string of rumoured and actual government anti-speculation measures.
Bengang was unlikely to fare better in the afternoon as investors were shunning the steel sector, analysts said.
"Who wants to buy steel when even the stronger sectors are caving in?" an analyst at a foreign investment bank said.

The steel company in June completed an initial public offering of 400 million B shares, carrying a P/E ratio of eight times based on fully diluted 1996 per-share net profit of 0.318 yuan under international accounting standards.
Many state-controlled steel companies, saddled with debt and bloated workforces, have been unable to compete since the introduction on market reforms in the late 1970s.
China has 2,000 steel factories, only 75 of which made a profit last year, analysts said.
Bengang's performance dragged other new shares down, with Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd and Beijing Orient Electronics losing on heavy volumes.
Chenming shed HK$0.29 to HK$6.50 on volume of 559,100 shares.
Beijing Orient lost HK$0.04 to HK$3.83 as 412,900 shares changed hands.
